```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Zaloumis et al. (2014) pooled the dihydroartemisinin (DHA) concentrations of
six studies of intravenous artesunate (ARS) in adults and children with severe
malaria and fitted a one-compartment model to DHA alone, assuming that ARS is
converted to DHA instantly and completely. The paper reports two final models
side by side in Table 3, each with its NONMEM code in the supplement, and both
are packaged:

* `Zaloumis_2014_artesunate` -- fitted to all 266 patients, including those who
  received IV ARS in period two of the three crossover trials. Covariates: body
  weight, age (maturation) and sex.
* `Zaloumis_2014_artesunate_period1` -- refitted to the 223 patients who
  received IV ARS at baseline. Stepwise selection then also retained admission
  hemoglobin and body temperature on clearance. The paper uses this model for
  its dose simulations (Figure 2) and for the exposure-response analysis
  (Table 4).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zaloumis_2014_artesunate"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2014.43> (open access, PMC4259998)

```{r models}
mod_all <- readModelDb("Zaloumis_2014_artesunate")
mod_p1 <- readModelDb("Zaloumis_2014_artesunate_period1")
```

# Population

The pooled data set holds 1,014 DHA concentrations from 266 patients (195
African children from Gabon, Malawi and Ghana; 71 adults from Bangladesh,
Thailand and Vietnam) with severe or moderately severe *Plasmodium falciparum*
malaria (Zaloumis 2014 Tables 1 and 2). Children had a median age of 3.47 years
(0.57-9.26) and weight of 13 kg (6-29), 52% male; adults a median age of 24
years (16-65) and weight of 50 kg (33-75), 58% male. Median admission
hemoglobin was 8.5 g/dL in children and 10.3 g/dL in adults, and median
temperature 38.0 and 38.3 degC. Most patients received 2.4 mg/kg IV ARS; one
arm of the largest study (Kremsner et al. 2012) received 4 mg/kg. Samples were
taken within 12 h of the dose.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Zaloumis_2014_artesunate")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value comes from Table 3 of the paper or the NONMEM code in the
Supplementary Information.

| Equation / parameter | All patients | Baseline IV only | Source location |
|----------------------|-------------:|-----------------:|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL, 15-kg female, L/h) | log(13.0) | log(12.9) | Table 3, population mean CL |
| `lvc` (V, 15-kg female, L) | log(11.56) | log(11.66) | Table 3, population mean V |
| `e_male_vc` | -0.14 | -0.15 | Table 3, beta V,MALE |
| `e_hgb_cl` (per g/dL from 8.8) | n/a | -0.04 | Table 3, beta CL,HB; centring value in footnote and code |
| `e_bodytemp_cl` (per degC from 38.2) | n/a | 0.07 | Table 3, beta CL,TEMP; centring value in footnote and code |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` variances | 0.59^2, 0.44^2 | 0.55^2, 0.42^2 | Table 3, SD of eta_CL and eta_V |
| `etalcl`-`etalvc` covariance | 0.61 x 0.59 x 0.44 | 0.60 x 0.55 x 0.42 | Table 3, correlation |
| `expSd` (Kremsner 2012) | 0.34 | 0.35 | Table 3, sigma_1 |
| `expSdKrishna2001` | 0.36 | 0.35 | Table 3, sigma_2 |
| `expSdNealon2002` | 0.43 | 0.44 | Table 3, sigma_3 |
| `expSdMaude2009` | 0.36 | 0.37 | Table 3, sigma_4 |
| `expSdWhoSimpson2006` | 0.30 | 0.33 | Table 3, sigma_5 |
| `expSdDavis2001` | 0.27 | 0.27 | Table 3, sigma_6 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Supplementary NONMEM code, `(WGT/WGTmed)**0.75`, `TVV*(WGT/WGTmed)`, `WGTmed = 15` |
| `cl_pna_famp` | 1/3.1 - 1 (fixed) | 1/3.1 - 1 (fixed) | Supplementary NONMEM code, `TVCL/3.1` weight on `EXP(-0.082*AGEmth)` |
| `lcl_pna_kdes` (1/month) | log(0.082) (fixed) | log(0.082) (fixed) | Supplementary NONMEM code, `EXP(-0.082*AGEmth)`, `AGEmth = AGE*12` |
| `f(central) = 284/384` | -- | -- | Methods, Pharmacokinetic modeling: DHA dose = 284/384 x ARS dose |
| `d/dt(central) = -cl/vc * central`; IV bolus | -- | -- | Results; NONMEM `ADVAN1` |
| `Cc ~ lnorm(...)` | -- | -- | Results ("additive error on the natural log scale"); NONMEM `Y = IPRED + W*EPS(1)`, `IPRED = LOG(F)` |

The clearance equation in the NONMEM code is

```
CL = ((TVCL/3.1) * (WGT/15)^0.75 * exp(-0.082*AGEmth) +
       TVCL * (WGT/15)^0.75 * (1 - exp(-0.082*AGEmth))) * exp(ETA(1))
```

which is `TVCL * (WGT/15)^0.75 * (1 + (1/3.1 - 1) * exp(-0.082*AGEmth))`: a
newborn has 1/3.1 of the mature clearance and the deficit decays at 0.082 per
month of age (half-life about 8.5 months).

# Typical-value profiles

```{r typical}
grid <- c(0, 0.083, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12)
no_study <- c(
  STUDY_KRISHNA2001 = 0, STUDY_NEALON2002 = 0, STUDY_MAUDE2009 = 0,
  STUDY_WHO_SIMPSON2006 = 0, STUDY_DAVIS2001 = 0
)

make_events <- function(cov, times = grid) {
  doses <- cov |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_mg, cmt = "central")
  obs <- cov |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  out <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
  for (nm in names(no_study)) out[[nm]] <- 0
  out
}

typ_cov <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~patient,                  ~WT, ~AGE, ~SEXF, ~HGB, ~BODYTEMP,
  1L,  "child 8 kg, 1.5 years",    8,  1.5,    1,  8.8,     38.2,
  2L,  "child 15 kg, 4 years",    15,  4.0,    1,  8.8,     38.2,
  3L,  "adult 50 kg, 25 years",   50, 25.0,    1,  8.8,     38.2
) |>
  mutate(dose_mg = 2.4 * WT)

# The residual SDs are thetas (study-specific), so zeroRe() finds no sigma to
# zero and says so; the omegas are zeroed, which is what matters here.
typ <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_all),
  make_events(typ_cov, times = seq(0, 12, by = 0.05)),
  keep = "patient", returnType = "data.frame"
))

ggplot(typ, aes(time, Cc, colour = patient)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after IV artesunate 2.4 mg/kg (h)", y = "DHA (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical DHA profiles, all-patients model (female)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The 15-kg typical patient has CL = 13.0 L/h and V = 11.56 L, a half-life of
`r signif(log(2) * 11.56 / 13.0, 3)` h; the closed-form one-compartment bolus
solution checks the solver exactly:

```{r typical-check}
chk <- typ |>
  filter(patient == "child 15 kg, 4 years", time %in% c(0.5, 1, 2)) |>
  mutate(
    mat = 1 + (1 / 3.1 - 1) * exp(-0.082 * 48),
    closed = 1000 * 2.4 * 15 * 284 / 384 / 11.56 *
      exp(-13.0 * mat / 11.56 * time)
  )
stopifnot(all(abs(chk$Cc / chk$closed - 1) < 1e-4))
knitr::kable(dplyr::select(chk, time, Cc, closed), digits = 1)
```

# Post hoc exposure in the pooled cohort (Table 3)

Table 3 gives the median post hoc DHA Cmax, AUC0-12h, half-life, CL/kg and
V/kg of the 266 patients for the all-patients model. The virtual cohort below
mirrors Table 2: 195 children and 71 adults with the published medians and
ranges. The paper does not tabulate the doses actually given; the cohort gives
4 mg/kg to 81 children (the Kremsner 4 mg/kg arm, matching the 81 patients the
exposure-response analysis excludes for a dose outside 2-3 mg/kg) and
2.4 mg/kg to everyone else.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2014)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2014)

# Bounded log-normal draw around a median, clipped to the published range.
draw <- function(z, med, sdlog, lo, hi) pmin(pmax(med * exp(sdlog * z), lo), hi)

z_child <- rnorm(195)
children <- tibble(
  id = 1:195,
  regimen = rep(c("child 2.4 mg/kg", "child 4 mg/kg"), c(114, 81)),
  WT = draw(z_child, 13, 0.35, 6, 29),
  AGE = draw(0.8 * z_child + 0.6 * rnorm(195), 3.47, 0.6, 0.57, 9.26),
  SEXF = rbinom(195, 1, 0.48),
  mg_per_kg = ifelse(regimen == "child 4 mg/kg", 4, 2.4)
)
adults <- tibble(
  id = 195 + 1:71,
  regimen = "adult 2.4 mg/kg",
  WT = draw(rnorm(71), 50, 0.18, 33, 75),
  AGE = draw(rnorm(71), 24, 0.35, 16, 65),
  SEXF = rbinom(71, 1, 0.42),
  mg_per_kg = 2.4
)
pooled_cov <- bind_rows(children, adults) |>
  mutate(dose_mg = mg_per_kg * WT)
pooled_events <- make_events(pooled_cov)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pooled_cov$id))

# DHA falls by up to 2^-40 over 12 h in the fastest-clearing subjects, below
# the default absolute tolerance, so the solver's noise would show up as
# small negative concentrations; tighten the tolerances.
sim_pooled <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_all, pooled_events,
  keep = c("regimen", "WT"), returnType = "data.frame",
  atol = 1e-16, rtol = 1e-10
)
```

## Simulated concentration-time percentiles (cf. Figure 1a)

Figure 1a is a visual predictive check against the observed data, which are not
public. The plot shows the simulated percentiles of log DHA (with residual
error, Kremsner residual SD) for the virtual pooled cohort.

```{r figure-1}
sim_pooled |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p025 = quantile(log(sim), 0.025),
    p50 = quantile(log(sim), 0.5),
    p975 = quantile(log(sim), 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p025, ymax = p975), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "log DHA (ng/mL)",
    title = "Simulated 2.5th, 50th and 97.5th percentiles",
    caption = "Simulation counterpart of Figure 1a of Zaloumis 2014."
  )
```

## PKNCA

```{r pknca}
# A handful of 12-h concentrations in the fastest-clearing subjects come back
# as -1e-15 ng/mL of solver round-off; check that is all they are and set
# them to zero so PKNCA does not warn about negative concentrations.
stopifnot(min(sim_pooled$Cc, na.rm = TRUE) > -1e-6)
nca_conc <- sim_pooled |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, regimen, time, Cc)

nca_dose <- pooled_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, regimen, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  nca_dose, amt ~ time | regimen + id,
  route = "intravascular"
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 12,
  cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals,
  options = list(auc.method = "lin up/log down")
))
```

The observation at time 0 is taken after the bolus, so `cmax` is the
post-dose concentration `dose x F / V`, which is what the NONMEM post hoc Cmax
of an `ADVAN1` bolus is. `lin up/log down` integrates the mono-exponential
decline without the linear-trapezoid overestimate.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tibble(
  cmax = 2946.6,
  auclast = 2560.3,
  half.life = 0.63
)
nca_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_long,
  reference = published,
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "h*ng/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Median post hoc DHA exposure, all-patients model: Table 3 of Zaloumis",
    "2014 against the virtual pooled cohort. AUClast is AUC0-12h.",
    "* differs by >20%."
  )
)

indiv <- sim_pooled |>
  filter(time == 12) |>
  transmute(id, regimen, cl_kg = cl / WT, v_kg = vc / WT)
param_cmp <- tibble::tibble(
  Parameter = c("CL (L/h/kg)", "V (L/kg)"),
  Published = c(0.76, 0.66),
  Simulated = c(median(indiv$cl_kg), median(indiv$v_kg))
) |>
  mutate(`% diff` = round(100 * (Simulated / Published - 1), 1))
knitr::kable(param_cmp, digits = 3, caption = "Median weight-normalised CL and V (Table 3 post hoc rows).")
```

```{r nca-assert}
nca_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(med = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE))
pct <- function(code, ref) 100 * (nca_med$med[nca_med$PPTESTCD == code] / ref - 1)
stopifnot(
  # The cohort is a reconstruction, and the published values are empirical
  # Bayes estimates shrunk toward the typical value (eta shrinkage 8% on CL,
  # 19% on V), so a 20% envelope on the centre is the right test: a
  # mistranscribed CL, V or dose conversion moves these by far more.
  abs(pct("cmax", 2946.6)) < 20,
  abs(pct("auclast", 2560.3)) < 20,
  abs(pct("half.life", 0.63)) < 20,
  abs(param_cmp$`% diff`) < 20
)
```

# Dose simulations in children and adults (Figure 2)

Figure 2 repeats, for IV ARS, the weight-band simulation that Hendriksen et al.
(2013) ran for IM ARS: AUC0-12h of DHA after the standard 2.4 mg/kg dose at
each body weight from 6 to 25 kg, and after the weight-band doses Hendriksen
proposed (Hendriksen 2013 Table 3). Supplementary Information 1 lists the
covariate distributions: within each weight band, age and hemoglobin uniform
over band-specific ranges, and temperature uniform on 35-40.1 degC. Those
inputs only enter the baseline-IV model, so it is the one simulated here.

For a one-compartment bolus, AUC0-12h is exactly
`dose x F / CL x (1 - exp(-CL/V x 12))`, so each subject's AUC is computed from
its simulated CL and V rather than from a concentration grid; 100 subjects per
kilogram keeps the band medians to a few percent of Monte Carlo error.

```{r figure-2-cohort}
set.seed(20142)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20142)

child_bands <- tibble::tibble(
  band = c("6-10 kg", "11-15 kg", "16-20 kg", "21-25 kg"),
  wt_lo = c(6, 11, 16, 21),
  age_lo = c(0.57, 1.45, 2.41, 5.45), age_hi = c(2.89, 5.88, 9.26, 9.09),
  hgb_lo = c(2.4, 4.33, 4.33, 8.6), hgb_hi = c(12.5, 13.3, 11.8, 11.3)
)
# Hendriksen 2013 Table 3: proposed IM dose (mg) by weight band.
proposed_mg <- function(wt) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    wt <= 7 ~ 20, wt <= 9 ~ 25, wt <= 11 ~ 30, wt <= 13 ~ 35,
    wt <= 16 ~ 40, wt <= 20 ~ 50, TRUE ~ 60
  )
}

n_per_kg <- 100
child_cov <- tidyr::crossing(WT = 6:25, rep = seq_len(n_per_kg)) |>
  mutate(b = findInterval(WT, child_bands$wt_lo)) |>
  mutate(
    band = child_bands$band[b],
    AGE = runif(n(), child_bands$age_lo[b], child_bands$age_hi[b]),
    HGB = runif(n(), child_bands$hgb_lo[b], child_bands$hgb_hi[b]),
    BODYTEMP = runif(n(), 35, 40.1),
    SEXF = rbinom(n(), 1, 0.5)
  ) |>
  select(-b, -rep)

adult_bands <- tibble::tibble(
  wt_lo = c(33, 45, 51, 61),
  age_lo = c(16, 16, 18, 21), age_hi = c(28, 27, 41, 65),
  hgb_lo = c(2.9, 6, 5.1, 6.5), hgb_hi = c(13.8, 13.1, 13.2, 15)
)
adult_cov <- tidyr::crossing(WT = seq(33, 75, by = 3), rep = seq_len(n_per_kg)) |>
  mutate(b = findInterval(WT, adult_bands$wt_lo)) |>
  mutate(
    band = "adults",
    AGE = runif(n(), adult_bands$age_lo[b], adult_bands$age_hi[b]),
    HGB = runif(n(), adult_bands$hgb_lo[b], adult_bands$hgb_hi[b]),
    BODYTEMP = runif(n(), 36.6, 40),
    SEXF = rbinom(n(), 1, 0.5)
  ) |>
  select(-b, -rep)

fig2_cov <- bind_rows(
  child_cov |> mutate(regimen = "Standard", dose_mg = 2.4 * WT),
  child_cov |> mutate(regimen = "Proposed", dose_mg = proposed_mg(WT)),
  adult_cov |> mutate(regimen = "Standard", dose_mg = 2.4 * WT)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_p1, make_events(fig2_cov, times = 12),
  keep = c("regimen", "band", "WT", "dose_mg"), returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  mutate(auc012 = 1000 * dose_mg * 284 / 384 / cl * (1 - exp(-cl / vc * 12)))
```

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 7}
fig2_sum <- fig2 |>
  group_by(panel = ifelse(band == "adults", "Adults", "Children"), regimen, WT) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(auc012),
    q25 = quantile(auc012, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(auc012, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ref_25kg <- fig2_sum$med[fig2_sum$regimen == "Standard" & fig2_sum$WT == 25]

ggplot(fig2_sum, aes(WT, med, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ref_25kg, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(panel, c("Children", "Adults")), ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Standard = "black", Proposed = "red")) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "DHA AUC0-12h (h x ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Zaloumis 2014 (median and 25th-75th percentiles)."
  )
```

The Results quote the median (25th-75th percentile) AUC0-12h after
2.4 mg/kg in each child weight band:

```{r figure-2-compare}
pub_bands <- tibble::tibble(
  band = c("6-10 kg", "11-15 kg", "16-20 kg", "21-25 kg"),
  pub_med = c(2077, 2127, 2122, 2426),
  pub_q25 = c(1403, 1442, 1443, 1669),
  pub_q75 = c(3124, 3063, 3094, 3517)
)
band_cmp <- fig2 |>
  filter(regimen == "Standard", band != "adults") |>
  group_by(band) |>
  summarise(
    sim_med = median(auc012),
    sim_q25 = quantile(auc012, 0.25),
    sim_q75 = quantile(auc012, 0.75),
    gm = exp(mean(log(auc012))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  inner_join(pub_bands, by = "band") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_med / pub_med - 1)) |>
  arrange(match(band, pub_bands$band))

band_cmp |>
  select(band, pub_med, sim_med, pct_diff, pub_q25, sim_q25, pub_q75, sim_q75) |>
  rename(
    "Weight band" = band, "Published median" = pub_med,
    "Simulated median" = sim_med, "% diff" = pct_diff,
    "Published Q25" = pub_q25, "Simulated Q25" = sim_q25,
    "Published Q75" = pub_q75, "Simulated Q75" = sim_q75
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "AUC0-12h (h x ng/mL) after 2.4 mg/kg IV ARS by weight band.")

gm_reduction <- 100 * (1 - band_cmp$gm[1] / band_cmp$gm[4])
```

The paper reports a 13.7% (95% CI 11.7-15.6%) lower geometric-mean AUC in
6-10 kg than in 21-25 kg children; the simulation gives
`r round(gm_reduction, 1)`%.

```{r figure-2-assert}
stopifnot(
  # Band medians of 500 subjects each carry about 3% Monte Carlo error; a
  # wrong maturation constant, centring value or dose conversion shifts them
  # by tens of percent.
  abs(median(band_cmp$pct_diff)) < 10,
  all(abs(band_cmp$pct_diff) < 20),
  gm_reduction > 5, gm_reduction < 25
)
```

The proposed weight-band regimen lifts the small-child exposures to the level
of the 25-kg children, and adults at 2.4 mg/kg sit at or above that level, as
in the paper's lower panel. The paper does not tabulate the adult medians; read
off its lower panel they rise from about 2,500 h x ng/mL at 33 kg to about
3,400 at 75 kg, and the simulated medians run roughly 10% higher over the same
range. The single-kilogram medians (100 subjects each) scatter by several
percent, which is also why the dashed 25-kg reference line sits a little above
the paper's.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Two final models.** Table 3 reports the all-patients fit and the refit
  without period-two crossover patients as parallel final models, each with
  NONMEM code; both are packaged. The paper's own simulations (Figure 2) use
  the baseline-IV model, since they draw hemoglobin and temperature.
- **ARS is not modelled.** As in the paper, the dose enters the DHA
  compartment as an IV bolus scaled by 284/384, the molecular-weight ratio the
  authors used (dose in mg of artesunate). Supply artesunate doses; the model
  converts them. The authors note this assumption overpredicts the DHA Cmax.
- **Study-specific residual error.** The six residual SDs are selected by five
  `STUDY_*` indicators with Kremsner et al. 2012 as the reference. They act on
  the residual error only; leave them at 0 for new populations.
- **Censoring.** The source analysis handled the 3.6% of samples below the
  study-specific LLOQ with the M3 method; simulation needs no counterpart.
- **Variance components.** Table 3 gives the IIV as SDs with a correlation.
  The Supplementary Table S1 column for subgroup 1 prints the same quantities
  as variances with the V variance (0.19) and the covariance (0.16)
  transposed; Table 3 is used.
- **Virtual cohorts.** The pooled cohort reconstructs Table 2 with bounded
  log-normal draws (children's age correlated with weight). The doses actually
  given are not tabulated; 81 children receive 4 mg/kg as described above.
  Sex is drawn 50:50 in the Figure 2 simulation, which Supplementary
  Information 1 does not specify; it only affects V. Study indicators are 0
  (Kremsner residual SD) throughout.
- **Table 1 dose for Davis et al.** Table 1 prints the Davis et al. regimens as
  120 and 240 "mg/kg"; this does not affect the model.
- **Errata.** Europe PMC lists no correction or erratum linked to this article
  (PMID 25372510), checked 2026-11-23.
